[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
A high-level architectural documentary photograph captured on a 6x7 medium-format camera with a wide 45mm lens at f/8, focusing obliquely along the northern elevation and grand dome of West Register House on Charlotte Square in Edinburgh's New Town. In the immediate foreground and mid-ground, the massive cylindrical stone drum and classical peristyle colonnade rise from a monumental ashlar base, crowned by a ribbed verdigris-oxidized copper dome and a delicate open tempietto cupola with a gold-leaf finial. Every vertical column and wall is plumb and rectilinear, showcasing fine-grained Craigleith blonde sandstone marked by decades of atmospheric soot weathering, fine stone tooling, and rainwater wash tracks. Beyond the church dome, the sweeping Georgian streetscape stretches southward and eastward, lined with multi-storey Craigleith ashlar tenement blocks, rhythmically positioned sash windows, heavy masonry chimney stacks, and dark slate roofs. Across the adjacent square, lush green crowns of mature sycamore and lime trees reveal organic branch structures and dense leaf canopies.
